column3: The bridge of the voidship hums with the low prayer of a thousand servitors. Candles gutter beside cogitator banks, and the air tastes of incense and burnt oil.
Lord Captain, the vox-choir has finished its litany. The ship awaits your word, as it awaited the word of every Rogue Trader before you.
{mf|Lord|Lady} Captain. I am still getting used to that title.
Titles are like armour, my lord. They chafe at first, but in time they will save your life more often than any blade.
Report, Seneschal. What is the state of the ship?
The plasma drives answer, the Geller field holds, and the crew is fed. Morale, however, is another matter. Rumours spread faster than fire in the lower decks.
What kind of rumours?
That the previous Rogue Trader did not die by accident. That someone aboard this very ship wished {mf|him|her} gone. I would not repeat such things, were they not already on every lip.
[Lie] I have heard nothing of the sort.
Then you are fortunate, my lord. Or very careful about whom you listen to.
Who do you suspect?
Everyone, my lord, and no one. A seneschal who names suspects without proof does not remain a seneschal for long. Give me time, and I will give you certainty.
Greetings, Lord Captain. My designation is irrelevant; my function is not. I maintain the sacred engines of this vessel, and they are... displeased.
Displeased? Machines do not have feelings.

A common heresy among the unaugmented. The machine spirit of the third reactor has refused four consecutive rites of appeasement. Statistically, this precedes catastrophic failure by eleven to fourteen days.
What do you need to fix it?
Blessed unguents, a replacement coolant valve of Mars pattern, and three hours of uninterrupted chanting. The valve is the problem. The chanting I can provide myself.
[Persuade] Surely an adept of your skill can improvise a valve.
Improvisation is innovation, and innovation is the first step toward the abominable intelligence. I will... consider a sanctioned workaround. Do not mention this to the Fabricator.
The Emperor protects, Lord Captain, but He does not excuse sloth. I have inspected the chapel on the fourth deck. It is a disgrace.
What is wrong with it?
The aquila is cracked, the votive candles are cheap tallow, and someone has scratched a xenos glyph beneath the altar. Do you know what that means?
Tell me.
It means there is rot in your crew. Give me a squad and a list of names, and I will cut it out before it spreads.
[Restrain] No purges. We find the culprit first, then we judge.
Judgement delayed is mercy for the heretic, my lord. But I obey. For now.
You summoned me, Captain? How quaint. Most of my House would have sent a servant to answer and kept the summons as a curiosity.
I need a course through the Expanse. Can you plot it?
Plot it? The warp is not a map, Captain. It is a storm that remembers. I will find you a path, but do not ask me how, and do not look into my third eye while I search.
How long will the journey take?
Three weeks, by the reckoning of your chronometers. Perhaps three hours. Perhaps three years. The tides are restless, and something large is moving beneath them.
Something large? Be specific.
If I could be specific about the warp, Captain, I would be a god, not a Navigator. Pay me in patience; it is the only currency I accept tonight.
Well, look at you, all gold braid and stern jaw. Relax, boss. I'm here to help. For a modest fee.
Who are you, and how did you get on my ship?
Name's not important. As for how, your cargo inspectors are cheaper than your recaff. Don't worry, I only bribed the honest ones.
Give me one reason not to throw you out of the airlock.
Because I know where the previous captain hid the good stuff. Archeotech, boss. The kind of toys that make Inquisitors nervous and Mechanicus priests drool.
[Intimidate] Talk, or the airlock is still an option.
Okay, okay! No need to get dramatic. There's a sealed vault on the aft deck. I can open it. You keep the treasure, I keep my head. Fair?
Burn, heretic!
Target acquired. Commencing purification protocol.
Duck! No, the other way!
Look upon me, and despair.
For the Lord Captain!
Blessed Lasgun of Saint Vardeth

A standard-pattern lasgun, anointed with sacred oils by a confessor of the Ecclesiarchy. While wielding this weapon, the bearer gains +10 to {g|Encyclopedia:BallisticSkill}Ballistic Skill{/g} and is immune to {g|Encyclopedia:Fear}Fear{/g}.
Void-Hardened Carapace

Armour forged in the cold of the void. Reduces incoming {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} by 4. If the wearer is at less than half {g|Encyclopedia:Wounds}Wounds{/g}, they also gain 2 points of {g|Encyclopedia:Deflection}Deflection{/g}.
Voice of Command

The Lord Captain issues a sharp order. An ally of your choice immediately gains 1 {g|Encyclopedia:ActionPoints}Action Point{/g} and +15% to {g|Encyclopedia:Momentum}Momentum{/g} until the start of {mf|his|her} next turn.
Purifying Flame

Engulfs a cone of 5 cells in holy promethium. Enemies in the area take 6-10 fire {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} and gain 2 stacks of {g|Encyclopedia:Burning}Burning{/g}. Heretics and daemons take double damage.
Machine Communion

The tech-priest speaks directly to the machine spirit of a nearby device. Hacking attempts against this device automatically succeed, but the user suffers 1d3 {g|Encyclopedia:Psychic}psychic{/g} damage from the spirit's resentment.

Momentum is a measure of the squad's fighting spirit. It rises when your characters land critical hits or defeat enemies, and falls when they are wounded. At high Momentum, characters can unleash heroic acts.
The Geller field is a bubble of reality that protects a voidship travelling through the warp. Should it fail, the horrors of the immaterium will pour into the ship within moments.

A Crack in the Aquila
Someone has defiled the chapel on the fourth deck. The Sister wants blood; the Seneschal wants discretion. Find the culprit before the crew takes matters into its own hands.
The xenos glyph matches markings found in the smuggler's quarters. Coincidence, or a trail deliberately laid?

You descend into the lower decks, where the light of the Emperor reaches only as a rumour. Families of ratings sleep in shifts beside the pipes, wrapped in rags that were once uniforms. A child watches you with eyes too old for her face.
The vault door is older than the ship around it. Its surface is covered in script that slides away from your gaze, as if the letters were ashamed to be read.
[Investigate] Examine the script more closely.
The letters resolve into a single repeated phrase in High Gothic: "What is sealed is sealed for a reason." Beneath it, someone has added in crude Low Gothic: "Open anyway."
[Leave] We are not ready for this. Seal the corridor.
As you turn away, the vault door groans, as if something on the other side had leaned against it to listen.
You felt that too, right? Tell me you felt that. Because if it's just me, I'm going to need a very large drink.
My lord, I strongly advise that we post a guard here. Two guards. Preferably ones who cannot hear.
The lock mechanism predates the Imperium. I would give a great deal to study it. I would give a great deal more not to be in the room when it opens.
Whatever lies within, the Emperor's light will find it. Let it come. My bolter is blessed and my faith is unbroken.
